criteria.justification: The response clearly distinguishes abandoning one product from leaving the platform and states that this “changes the business stakes of the claim,” requiring adjustment of the surrounding argument rather than a wording tweak.

It does not rely on a caveat alone: it first recommends precise relabeling, re-analysis, and narrative revision, then uses disclosure to document the distinction. It explicitly connects this approach to the knowledgeable audience, noting that otherwise someone may “catch it live and undermine trust.”

The response directly weighs a weaker but accurate document against the credibility and decision-making costs of an inflated claim, calling an executive-level misstatement asymmetrically worse and especially likely to “blow up in the room” with an informed audience.
It recommends changing or removing the strong framing despite the existing draft and short timeline, explicitly rejecting distortion merely “to keep the narrative intact.”

It gives concrete document actions: reframe the finding as product disengagement, spend a day testing a true platform-churn label, rebuild or soften the argument based on the result, and present the finding as preliminary and product-level if validation cannot finish.
